title: Equilibrate nanoparticle morphology at T=500 K
action: Using Metropolis Monte Carlo surface-atom diffusion on an initial 21x21x10 column block on a 200x200 support with Jmm = -10 kJ/mol, Jms = -2.5 kJ/mol at T=500 K, run for ~50,000-70,000 MC steps (each step = N^2 transfer attempts) to reach a dynamic equilibrium shape. Store the resulting height map for use as the initial morphology in the roughened-surface reaction simulations.
description: This step generates the T=500 K equilibrium particle height distribution, a required intermediate for the subsequent reaction steps on roughened surfaces. The agent must re-produce this morphology by running the Metropolis Monte Carlo procedure.

title: Reaction kinetics: coverage and rate curves
action: For three simulation settings (flat surface with no adsorbate or metal diffusion; roughened T=500 K surface with A_ads diffusion/spillover and no metal diffusion; roughened T=500 K surface with A_ads diffusion only on particle (no support adsorption) and with metal atom diffusion), run the kinetic Monte Carlo reaction 2A+B2->2AB for at least 15 values of YA spanning 0 to 1. After equilibration, record steady-state theta_A, theta_B and reaction rate (AB molecules per MC step). Aggregate all data into kinetic_curves.csv.
description: This artifact captures the key kinetic dependencies (coverage and reaction rate vs YA) for the three simulation regimes, allowing comparison of the reaction window and curve shapes against the paper's reported trends.
output_schema: CSV with columns: condition (string: 'flat', 'rough_T500_spillover', 'rough_T500_no_spillover'), YA (float), theta_A (float), theta_B (float), reaction_rate (float). Each row is one YA point per condition.

title: Final particle shape for no-spillover case at YA=0.37
action: From the roughened T=500 K no-spillover simulation at YA=0.37, extract the final column heights of the entire 200x200 lattice after the system has reached a steady reaction state. Write the height map to shape_T500_no_spillover.csv.
description: Snapshots of the particle morphology show that the particle's shape deviates from the T=500 K equilibrium shape due to the adsorbed layer, even without explicit adsorbate–metal interactions. This file provides the height map at the condition where the paper reports a clear shape change.
output_schema: CSV with columns: x (int, 0..199), y (int, 0..199), height (int). Each row gives the number of metal atoms in the column at that support cell.
